answers.how: Callisto travels approximately 86 pixels along its orbit in 3.30 s. Its known speed gives a scale of about 0.024 m/pixel; its diameter is approximately 4.4 pixels.
Jupiter's diameter is approximately 73 pixels. Multiplying by the Callisto-calibrated scale of 0.024 m/pixel gives 1.75 m.
Tracking Io along its circular orbit gives approximately 84 pixels/s. Using the Callisto-calibrated scale of 0.024 m/pixel gives 2.02 m/s.
Europa's measured orbital motion is approximately 54.6 pixels/s. Multiplying by 0.024 m/pixel gives 1.31 m/s.
Ganymede's measured orbital motion is approximately 35.9 pixels/s. Multiplying by 0.024 m/pixel gives 0.863 m/s.
Io's diameter is approximately 4.4 pixels, converted using the Callisto-calibrated scale of 0.024 m/pixel.
Europa's diameter is approximately 5.3 pixels, converted using the Callisto-calibrated scale of 0.024 m/pixel.
Ganymede's diameter is approximately 4.8 pixels, converted using the Callisto-calibrated scale of 0.024 m/pixel.
Io's orbital diameter is approximately 143 pixels. Multiplying by 0.024 m/pixel gives 3.43 m.
Europa's orbital diameter is approximately 183 pixels. Multiplying by 0.024 m/pixel gives 4.39 m.
Ganymede's orbital diameter is approximately 240 pixels. Applying the Callisto-calibrated scale gives about 5.77 m.
Callisto's orbital diameter is approximately 370 pixels. Multiplying by the motion-calibrated scale of 0.024 m/pixel gives 8.88 m.
